summary: Transport authored event markers through a separate manifest and dispatch them by interval crossing, because clip lifecycle events do not represent arbitrary marker payloads.
objective: Footsteps, cues and interaction beats fire once under forward/reverse playback, wrapping, large time steps, seeks and interruptions according to declared policy.
applies_when: Animation timing must trigger sounds, particles, state changes or interaction windows.
Blender markers are used as authoring cues for a glTF animation.
intent_signals: export Blender timeline markers as runtime events
avoid duplicate footsteps at loop wrap
example_prompts: Author named footfall markers in Blender and consume a sidecar event manifest in Three.js.
Define whether a scrub or interrupted clip fires skipped animation cues.
negative_signals: Assuming Blender marker names become core glTF animation channels.
Using only mixer loop and finished events for arbitrary in-clip cues.
not_for: Authoritative gameplay events that cannot depend on presentation timing.

principles: Core glTF animation expresses sampled property channels, not a general event-marker stream. Treat named Blender markers as source annotations and export a versioned sidecar or reviewed extras convention with clip identity and normalized or second-based time.

Dispatch arbitrary cues from time-interval crossings. The policy must cover forward and negative playback, exact endpoints, wrap, ping-pong, multiple loops crossed in one update, seeks, pauses and clip interruption.
Three.js mixer loop and finished events describe action lifecycle. They can help partition traversal, but do not replace the application marker manifest.
implementation: In Blender, name markers uniquely within their scope, associate them with the intended action/clip, and record the source frame rate when converting whole-frame positions to seconds.

At runtime, retain previous and current local clip time plus loop count/parity and traversal sign. Enumerate every crossed marker in effective evaluated-clip order: `(previous,current]` forward and `[current,previous)` reverse, splitting every wrapped interval and assigning a stable marker ID plus loop iteration for deduplication. Under LoopPingPong, derive effective clip direction from loop parity as well as playback sign; signed loopDelta reports crossed boundaries but does not alone identify the alternating evaluated direction.

Declare seek and interruption behavior per event class: suppress cosmetic events during scrub, optionally reconstruct stateful windows from absolute time, and never replay a one-shot merely because a blend reevaluates the same pose.
observable_checks: A fixture with two markers crossed in one large update emits both in traversal order, once each.

Forward wrap, reverse wrap and multiple-boundary steps produce the declared sequence without missing or duplicating the seam marker; LoopPingPong tests derive alternating effective direction from parity rather than treating signed loopDelta as sufficient.
Scrub, pause/resume and mid-clip interruption match the manifest policy, while Three.js loop/finished listeners remain identifiable as lifecycle events.

creative_affordances: Events may drive footsteps, sparks, subtitles, musical accents, squash anticipation or ritual cues.
The manifest may use frames, seconds or normalized phase when conversion and clip identity are explicit.
known_limits: Blender markers occur on whole frames, limiting subframe authoring precision in the cited interface.
Sidecar or extras schemas are application conventions, not core glTF guarantees.
No marker exporter or event dispatcher was run.

claims.statement: Blender markers denote significant animation frames, carry names, and are placed at whole frame numbers; pose markers are specific to armatures and shape keys.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 marker authoring only; export transport is not asserted.
